On Thursday, the BCI had initially directed state bar councils not to enrol any students from NALSAR’s 2026 graduating batch as advocates. However, within a couple of hours of issuing the directive, the BCI issued a second letter to NALSAR Vice-Chancellor Professor Srikrishna Deva Rao and all state bar councils, rescinding its earlier order. items.title: ‘Genuine’ vs ‘political’: The social media campaign pitting Ranchi protests against CJP
items.summary: As Jharkhand’s student protest against alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) builds momentum in Ranchi, sections on social media have tried to cast it as the ‘genuine’ counterpart to the Cockroach Janta Party-led protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, the one ‘without foreign funding’ and ‘led by students’. Even when protesters on the ground, and the evidence itself, tell a different story of shared solidarity and mutual inspiration, not rivalry. Using specific keywords, Newslaundry conducted searches across Facebook and X to track online discussions around the two protests. This analysis identified recurring narratives praising the Jharkhand protest while contrasting it with CJP's month-long protest against the NEET-UG exam paper leak in Delhi that ended with Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation on July 25. The CJP protest faced allegations of foreign funding, political backing, ‘Azadi’ slogans and violence. Same accounts, different angle At least two posts followed identical templates and were traced back to accounts that had separately criticised CJP. One Facebook post read: “Student power is a wave of the people – no hooliganism, no shouting, no inflammatory statements, no stone-throwing, no anti-national talk. No abuse. Just students peacefully protesting for their rights, focused on student interests.” The post went on to allege that Jharkhand Police had “brutally lathi-charged” students and questioned why political leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and Arvind Kejriwal, had remained silent. The post was shared at least 20 times on Facebook between August 10 and 12. Different users shared the same template, accompanied by visuals of students marching through Ranchi. The post never names CJP, but its checklist – peaceful, student-led, free of ‘anti-national’ slogans – reads as direct rebuttal to it. Newslaundry then tracked some of the accounts that had shared the post to examine whether they had also participated in online discussions around the CJP protest. items.title: The crisis after the flood in Assam villages: Lost livestock, missed crop, and wait for aid
items.summary: When the floodwaters rose around their home in Rajapul on July 19, Bandana Buragohain had no way of getting out on her own. The 70-year-old clung to the back of a man from her village as he waded into the current. At one point, the force of the water pushed him backwards. A couple of other boys came and helped carry her to a nearby house with a terrace, where around 30 others had already taken shelter. “I somehow managed to stay alive. I could have died,” she recalled. Rajapul, in the Nazira subdivision of Sivasagar district, was among the areas caught in the path of what several reports have described as one of Assam's worst localised floods since the 1950s. After days of heavy rain across the region, including 137 mm recorded over eight to nine hours in the neighbouring hills of Nagaland , a sudden rush of water moved downstream into the plains on July 19, sending the Dikhow, Disang and Janji, rivers that eventually meet the Brahmaputra, above extreme flood levels within hours and engulfing settlements before families could evacuate. The same rainfall triggered multiple landslides in Nagaland’s Mon district, killing nine people. The death toll climbed to 100, with more than 2.12 lakh people affected across Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Golaghat districts. Livestock losses were extensive, and 17,198 hectares of agricultural land were submerged. Within Sivasagar district, Nepali Khuti in Bihubar emerged as the epicentre of the disaster, with more than 300 families left destitute. Videos from the village showed bodies being recovered from beneath layers of silt. Weeks on, the water has drained out of most of Sivasagar, but little else has been restored. For families in the affected villages, the livestock is gone, the sowing window has passed, and many still wait for cash assistance. items.title: Delhi High Court refuses to stop private channel from broadcasting Gurbani from Golden Temple
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday refused to pass any interim orders on a plea filed by Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) to stop a private television channel from broadcasting or rebroadcasting Gurbani (sacred hymns and scriptures of Sikhism) from the Golden Temple. SGPC and a channel named PTC approached the High Court against Galactic Television and Communications alleging copyright infringement. SGPC – the apex body entrusted with managing the Golden Temple (Sri Harmandir Sahib) – argued that they hold the copyright in the broadcast of the Gurbani from the Golden Temple. It stated that Galactic Television, by broadcasting the same, although with a 10-second delay, is violating their rights. At present, the Gurbani from the Golden Temple is broadcast on SGPC’s YouTube channel and on PTC. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani today gave a prima facie opinion that the Guru Granth Sahib is a literary work and that if its broadcast by SGPC is used for a genuine religious ceremony without resorting to commercialisation, it may not amount to copyright infringement. “It is a literary cum musical work. You are reciting the Gurbani by way of musical performance. There is a literary work called Guru Granth Sahib which you sing by way of musical work. Therefore, you are a literary and a musical work which, if used for bona fide religious ceremony, is not an infringement,” the Court remarked. It agreed with the defendant Galactic Television’s submission that the broadcast by them may be exempt from copyright under Section 52(1)(z)(a) as also on a reading of Section 52 1(l) of the Copyright Act. “In view thereof, this Court is not inclined to pass any ad interim order at this stage,” the Bench said. The Bench asked the defendants to file their replies on the interim injunction application and said the case will be heard next on September 24. Anup Jairam Bhambhani Earlier, Senior Advocate Chander M Lall appeared for SGPC and argued that defendants’ actions do not amount to fair dealing. However, Senior Advocate PS Patwalia appeared for Galactic Television and argued that they are not commercialising the broadcast and that there is no copyright in the Gurbani or kirtan being streamed from the Golden Temple.

The petition filed by advocate K Balu, president of the Advocates’ Forum for Social Justice, has sought an interim injunction restraining TASMAC from operating its online booking portal and QR code-based collection mechanism. items.title: Understanding the intelligence pyramid: Why most businesses know everything and do nothing?
items.summary: In every consequential field of human endeavour, whether in the boardroom, the courtroom, or on the trading floor, one resource has consistently separated those who prevail from those who do not. The resource is intelligence: information that has been processed, placed in context, and converted into a decision within the window in which that decision still counts. Military history makes the point plainly. The intelligence failures that determined the outcomes of wars were rarely failures of collection; the signals were usually present. What failed was the architecture to convert those signals into understanding, and the discipline to act before the moment passed. Corporate history repeats the lesson, and increasingly, so does the law. When a regulator, a court, or a shareholder examines how an organisation behaved before a loss crystallised, the question is seldom whether the information existed. It is whether the organisation recognised what it held and converted that knowledge into a reasoned, recorded decision, or allowed it to travel no further than the report in which it arrived. In India, Section 166 of the Companies Act, 2013 requires directors to act in good faith and to exercise due and reasonable care, skill, and diligence, a standard against which a board's conduct is later assessed with the benefit of hindsight. This framing is more instructive. And it is the framing of the Intelligence Pyramid , a framework developed by IIRIS, that is designed to address. Directors' duties and the architecture of decision-making The Intelligence Pyramid categorizes enterprise intelligence into three levels: Strategic, Tactical, and Operational . The basic principle behind the intelligence pyramid is that intelligence needs to flow continuously and bidirectionally through all three levels. The minute that process gets broken down due to departmental silos, conflicting incentives, or poor infrastructure, it is not just an issue of becoming less responsive but one of creating liabilities. items.title: Supreme Court stays Madras HC order scrapping government jobs to Karur stampede victims’ families
items.summary: The Supreme Court Friday stayed Madras High Court's recent decision to quash the State government's decision to give jobs on compassionate grounds to the family members of the 41 persons killed in the September 2025 Karur stamped. A Bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran passed the interim order on a petition moved by the State government. "Issue notice. Judgment passed by the High Court shall remain stayed," the top court said. The apex court observed that an unfortunate incident had led the government to offer employment to the victim families. "Stampede took placed. Unfortunate incident happened. The government has decided to compensate them. Should government not give employment?," the Bench remarked. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran Senior Advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi , assisted by advocate Vrinda Bhandari, represented the State government. Abhishek Singhvi Last month, the High Court had ruled that the appointments could not be sustained since public employment must be made in accordance with Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution. The Bench noted that several other persons, whose family members had died while in government service, were already waiting for compassionate appointments. The State could not overlook those claims and give jobs to the families of those killed in the stampede, it added. The High Court passed the judgment on petitions challenging the government’s decision to offer employment to the families of the 41 persons who died in the September 2025 stampede at a Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) rally in Karur. The tragedy is presently being investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). After the TVK led by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay came to power following the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections held in April 2026, the State decided to give jobs to the kin of those who died in the stampede. The petitions before the High Court argued that compassionate appointments are ordinarily governed by strict rules applicable to the dependants of government employees who die while in service. It was also argued that the families had already received ex gratia compensation and granting employment while the CBI investigation was pending, could influence material witnesses. Social media platforms are no longer limited to communication and entertainment. They have evolved into sophisticated commercial ecosystems where businesses promote products, interact with consumers, complete transactions, and cultivate long term customer relationships. Platforms offering live shopping, influencer collaborations, short video marketing, and integrated purchasing features have transformed the commercial landscape across India. This evolution has created significant opportunities for businesses of every size. Brand owners increasingly confront infringement occurring through influencer content, fake business profiles, copied product images, misleading advertisements, counterfeit listings, and fraudulent social media accounts. Indian trademark jurisprudence has progressively evolved to address these commercial realities. Courts have consistently recognised trademarks as valuable commercial assets deserving robust legal protection. Judicial interpretation now extends beyond conventional physical marketplaces and increasingly reflects the realities of digital commerce and evolving consumer behaviour. items.title: Tripura High Court refuses to quash  case against content creator Madhabi Biswas who mocked PM Modi
items.summary: The Tripura High Court on Wednesday refused to quash criminal defamation and IT Act charges against content creator Madhabi Biswas Chakraborty over allegedly derogatory posts about the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Agartala's Mayor Dipak Majumdar and deity Mata Tripureshwari [Madhabi Biswas Chakraborty @ Madhavi Biswas Chakraborty @ Moon Moon Biswas vs State of Tripura & ors.]. A Division Bench of Justice T Amarnath Goud and Justice S Datta Purkayastha was hearing two petitions seeking quashing of FIRs registered at East Agartala and West Agartala police stations under Sections 356 of the BNS (defamation) and Section 67 of the Information Technology Act (publishing obscene material online). The Court held that at the quashing stage, its task is confined to examining whether the FIR and charge-sheet prima facie disclose the ingredients of an offence. It cannot conduct a mini-trial or assess whether the allegations would ultimately hold up at trial. It found that the petitioner's statements had prima facie drawn criticism of the Prime Minister and the Mayor by mocking their names, and had hurt religious sentiment connected to Mata Tripureshwari. This was sufficient to constitute defamation and entitle the complainants to sue. The Bench also noted that the investigation was incomplete, although the investigating officer had seized the petitioner's mobile phone, the underlying video clips or screen recordings could not be retrieved, and further time had been sought to produce them before the trial court. Since Section 193(9) of the BNSS permits further investigation even after a chargesheet has been filed, the Court held that the police remained free to recover the missing material including from cloud backups or deleted data and file a supplementary charge-sheet if warranted, without needing a fresh direction from the Court. The Court rejected the argument that free speech under Article 19(1)(a) shielded the petitioner's posts. Defamation, the Court said, operates as a reasonable restriction under Article 19(2), and that free expression does not license harm to reputation. It relied on the Supreme Court's rulings in Abhishek Singh v. Ajay Kumar and Somjeet Mallick v. State of Jharkhand to hold that an FIR need not be an exhaustive account of every allegation, and that courts must look at the overall gravamen of the accusations rather than isolated omissions. items.title: Allahabad High Court rejects woman’s plea seeking maternity leave for fourth child
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently dismissed a plea filed by a woman government employee seeking six months' maternity leave for her fourth child [Sashi Kumari v. State of UP and Others] Justice Manju Rani Chauhan passed the order on August 7 in a petition challenging a June 19 order by the government authorities who had rejected her claim for maternity leave for her fourth child. The petitioner argued that she had not availed maternity leave when her first three children were born and was therefore, entitled to the benefit for the fourth child since she was seeking maternity leave for the first time. The State opposed the plea, relying on the provisions of the Financial Handbook. It submitted that she was not entitled to maternity leave for her fourth child. Justice Manju Rani Chauhan The provision states that maternity leave is available to permanent or temporary women government employees for two occasions. It further provides that where a woman government employee has two or more living children, maternity leave cannot be granted. The Court, therefore, found no reason to interfere with the decision and rejected the petitioner's claim. "In view of the above, no interference is required by this Court," the Court said. Meanwhile, the Court flagged that only typed copies of documents had been annexed with the petition instead of photocopies of the original documents. The Court said it was difficult to decide issues on the basis of typed copies as they contain typing errors that needed to be verified against the original documents. Accordingly, the Court directed the reporting section to raise objections in such cases and ensure that writ petitions are filed with proper photocopies of the documents annexed to them. Today, a single case of banking fraud could involve internal surveillance units, external forensic analysts, police departments, enforcement agencies, lawyers, and regulatory reporting requirements, all working in parallel. items.title: The two halves of trust: Why DPDP compliance is more than a legal puzzle
items.summary: Imagine commissioning a state-of-the-art skyscraper. The architect delivers a brilliant blueprint: a design that is elegant, compliant with all building codes, and visionary in its scope. The legal team ensures all contracts are sound and permits are in order. But without an engineer to translate those plans into structural realities, without a construction crew to pour the foundation and erect the steel, the blueprint remains just that: a brilliant but unrealized idea. As India embarks on its journey to full DPDP Act compliance, many organizations find themselves in a similar position. They have the legal blueprint, meticulously crafted by expert counsel. They understand the articles of the law, the definitions, and the penalties. Yet, the chasm between understanding the law and implementing it on the ground remains vast. The notification of the DPDP Rules has started an 18-month countdown, and closing this gap has become the most pressing challenge for businesses and the legal professionals who guide them. Lawyers are the masters of the blueprint. From advising on the nuances of "free, specific, informed, and unconditional consent" to representing clients before the Data Protection Board, their expertise is non-negotiable. They must interpret the grounds for processing personal data, clarify the scope of legitimate uses, and define the boundaries of data processor engagement. items.title: Beyond collection: Making Chennai’s solid waste management a shared responsibility
items.summary: Every day, Chennai faces the daunting task of managing more than 6,000 tonnes of municipal solid waste generated by an estimated 7.4 million people. Ensuring that this waste is segregated at source and managed scientifically remains one of the city’s most persistent challenges. Recent reforms have sought to place greater responsibility on waste generators and promote decentralised waste management. Yet some of the city administration’s emerging responses appear to move in the opposite direction by further centralising collection and processing. This raises a fundamental question: are Chennai’s waste reforms genuinely shifting responsibility to the source, or further centralising waste management? The consequences of relying predominantly on centralised collection and disposal are already evident. For decades, much of Chennai’s waste was neither adequately segregated nor scientifically processed. For over 40 years, mixed waste was dumped at the Kodungaiyur and Perungudi dumpsites, which receive waste from north and south Chennai respectively. The result is severe ecological damage and a public health crisis for surrounding communities. The city’s waste has also found its way into waterways and along the coastline, polluting coastal waters and further exposing the weaknesses of its collection and disposal systems. In recent years, the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has taken concerted steps to contain some of the environmental damage caused by decades of indiscriminate dumping. At Perungudi, GCC has begun biomining legacy waste spread across nearly 200 acres. The initiative seeks to recover usable materials, safely dispose of what remains, and reclaim the land. Nearly 100 acres have reportedly been recovered so far. Given the dumpsite’s proximity to the Pallikaranai marsh, restoring the site could also help protect the surrounding wetland ecosystem. Similar efforts are underway at the 270-acre Kodungaiyur dumpsite. However, plans to establish new waste processing facilities there, including a proposed waste to energy (WTE) plant, have faced strong opposition from local communities. Residents have raised concerns about toxic emissions, groundwater contamination, and the further concentration of polluting infrastructure in an area that has already borne the burden of the city’s waste for decades. Niranjana N Nair, the daughter of the late Kannur Additional District Magistrate (ADM) K Naveen Babu, has been appointed as a Food Safety Officer in the Food Safety Department. The appointment was made under the Compassionate Employment Scheme (Ashrita Niyamanam) by the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Kerala. K Naveen Babu, who served as the ADM in Kannur district, died by suicide in October 2024 following public corruption allegations at a farewell meeting, which sparked a major political controversy in the state. The decision to appoint Naveen’s daughter to a government job was made at June’s cabinet meeting. On June 4, the government also issued an order granting Niranjana a dependent appointment. In the same meeting, the government decided to hand over the investigation into the death of Naveen Babu to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). The decision was taken following repeated demands from the deceased officer's family seeking a central agency probe into the case. Chief Minister VD Satheesan shared the picture with Naveen’s family on X. “The government keeps its word. The Telangana government’s call to auction 10.63 acres of prime real estate in Hyderabad’s IT corridor for a minimum of Rs 1,860 crore has triggered criticism as the plots lie right next to the Durgam Cheruvu lake. Critics have expressed concern that the land falls within the lake’s catchment area and is also close to heritage hillocks protected by the Hyderabad Urban Development Authority Zoning Regulations 1981. The e-auction of the two adjacent plots, part of the Raidurg Hyderabad Knowledge City, is scheduled for August 21 and 28, the Telangana State Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) has announced. The plots in survey no. 83/1 – 5.25 acres and 5.38 acres – fall under the Raidurg Panmaktha village of Serilingampally mandal. The TGIIC has set a minimum price of Rs 175 crore per acre for the auction. The Corporation also said that the site boundaries depicted in images in its auction brochure were only representative, and the exact land extent would be determined through a joint survey along with the successful bidder. However, the geographic coordinates of the auction site shows that it is barely 300 metres from the lake. Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) leader T Harish Rao wrote to Chief Minister Revanth Reddy asking him to cancel the auction, saying the land was a heritage site. The rocks surrounding Durga Cheruvu are nearly 2.5 billion years old. There were also competing claims of ownership over the land by the State Bank of India (SBI) and the Waqf Board, he said. He also pointed out that back in 2020, when CM Revanth was in the Opposition as a Congress MP, he had moved the High Court against the allocation of around 31 acres of land to real estate developer DLF in the same Raidurg area. items.title: Delimitation: CM Vijay writes to PM Modi, urges freeze on Lok Sabha seats at 543
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on August 13, urging the Union government to permanently freeze the Lok Sabha’s strength at 543 and retain the existing distribution of seats among states and Union Territories. In his letter, the Chief Minister pointed out the resolution adopted by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on August 12, which called for constitutional amendments to preserve the existing level of representation for states. “The existing number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to the states should be made permanent at the current level. Current distribution of seats among the states must be maintained. I kindly request you to consider the resolution passed by Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and bring necessary Constitutional amendments in this regard,” Vijay said in his letter. The Assembly resolution also sought the implementation of 33% reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha without changing the existing strength of 543. According to the resolution, the southern states could lose a significant number of parliamentary seats after population census if Article 81(2)(a) is applied. The Assembly cited the 1967 delimitation, when Tamil Nadu's Lok Sabha representation was reduced from 41 seats to 39. Vijay said any delimitation based on the post-1971 population that changes the existing strength of the states would cause “lasting injustice” to the southern states. He pointed out that these states had implemented population-control programmes and achieved economic growth while also carrying out healthcare and public welfare measures. The resolution was backed by the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the TVK’s coalition partners, while the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK), Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK), Desiya Murupokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK), and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) opposed it.

Three youngsters allegedly abducted, handed over to police, for mocking TDP MLA on WhatsApp
items.summary: In a shocking incident, three youngsters were allegedly abducted by henchmen of Gajapathinagaram MLA K Appala Naidu for mocking him over WhatsApp. After the abduction, the youngsters were later handed over to police, who arrested them. The arrested youngsters printed pamphlets with photos of the TDP MLA Appala Naidu with the message, “MLA is missing. Whether or not he is alive?” (sic). They then shared the image on WhatsApp, as a form of protest, to point out that the MLA had not fulfilled his poll promises, The Hindu reported. As the photo was widely shared on social media, TDP supporters filed a complaint with the police. The Times of India reported that the youth were kidnapped on Thursday and were handed over to police, the next day. The youngsters were arrested under Section 41 of the CRPC (cognizable offence) based on the complaint by TDP leader Ravi Sridhar. This comes after the Andhra government has been cracking down on people posting 'objectionable' content on social media, against the state's ruling TDP. In May, the Visakhapatnam police picked up a Bengaluru-based software professional, Ippala Ravindra, after he allegedly posted some objectionable comments against Payakaraopeta MLA V Anitha. Reports stated that Ravindra was apprehended under the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act, and not under the IT Act, as the legislator is also a Dalit. Many people claimed that Ravindra was on the YSRCP's payroll, as his page was filled with material that supported the party and YS Jagan. However, the party denied the allegations. This arrest also came one week after the Andhra police arrested political satirist Ravi Kiran, after the same MLA filed a complaint against a 'defamatory' post on his Facebook page. Ravi Kiran runs a Facebook page called 'Political Punch', which has more than 1 lakh followers, and is popular among critics of the ruling Telugu Desam Party (TDP). Many people have pointed out that several posts on the Facebook page 'Political Punch', were insensitive, and in bad taste. Ravi Kiran claimed that he was being targeted by the TDP government, because he was criticising them. Editor’s note: Some names have been removed upon request.
